name: United States
oneLiner: Meyer finds it egalitarian in manner but fast and top-down in decisions, and many of the examples involve written docs and blameless reviews.
intro: Most of the evidence for the United States comes from documents that large tech companies such as Google and Amazon published themselves, plus national statistics and surveys. Regulated industries and smaller companies are underrepresented as a result. The patterns below are country-level tendencies, and organizations and individuals vary widely.

design.text: At Google, engineers write a relatively informal design doc before they write code. Malte Ubl (2020) says its purpose is to record the trade-offs and alternatives the team considered, and that it is not meant to be an exhaustive specification.

sources.title: Design Docs at Google (Malte Ubl)

design.text: Ubl says a design doc should be as long as necessary and as short as possible, and distinguishes it from a heavyweight waterfall-style specification.

sources.title: Design docs - A design doc (Malte Ubl)

design.text: Meyer places the United States on the applications-first side of the Persuading scale. A book summary says this means starting from conclusions and examples, and caring more about the practical how than the theoretical why.

sources.title: The Investor's Podcast: The Culture Map Summary

failure.text: The Google SRE Book (2016) codifies the blameless postmortem. It identifies contributing causes without blaming individuals or teams and assumes that everyone involved acted with good intentions.

sources.title: Google SRE Book: Postmortem Culture

failure.text: At F8 in 2014, Zuckerberg changed Facebook's motto from "Move fast and break things" to "Move fast with stable infra." He said that at Facebook's scale, the time spent fixing breakage outweighed the gain in speed.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Facebook Themes f8 Around A Stable Mobile Platform

feedback.text: According to Meyer, Americans are often taught to wrap negative messages in positive ones (the feedback sandwich). She therefore places the United States in the middle of the scale for delivering negative feedback.

sources.title: Erin Meyer: How To Say "This Is Crap" In Different Cultures

feedback.text: A blog explainer on Meyer's Evaluating scale describes a common mismatch. Dutch and German colleagues take American praise at face value, and Americans find Dutch and German criticism too harsh.

sources.title: 4squareviews: The Evaluation Scale on the Cultural Map

feedback.text: A study of more than 70,000 GitHub pull requests from 17 countries (Rastogi et al., 2018) found that pull requests were more likely to be accepted when the reviewer and the submitter were in the same country.

sources.title: Rastogi et al.: Relationship between geographical location and evaluation of developer contributions in GitHub

hierarchy.text: Meyer classifies the United States as egalitarian but top-down (HBR, 2017). People use first names and are encouraged to speak up, but the boss decides quickly, and the decision can be reopened when new arguments appear.

sources.title: Erin Meyer: Being the Boss in Brussels, Boston, and Beijing (HBR)

hierarchy.text: In the same article, Meyer reports that to Japanese managers an American boss can look flat on the surface yet highly autocratic in how decisions are made.

sources.title: Erin Meyer: Being the Boss in Brussels, Boston, and Beijing (HBR)

communication.text: Meyer places the United States at the most low-context end of the Communicating scale. A book summary says Americans prefer to say things explicitly and to repeat and summarize key points.

sources.title: lifeclub: The Culture Map Summary

communication.text: According to Bezos's 2017 shareholder letter, Amazon does not use PowerPoint. Meetings start with everyone silently reading a six-page narrative memo, and memos carry no author's name because they come from the whole team.

sources.title: Amazon 2017 Letter to Shareholders

communication.text: CNBC (2018) traces the practice to a 2004 email from Bezos. He wrote that a good four-page memo is harder to write than a 20-page slide deck, because the narrative structure forces better thinking.

sources.title: CNBC: Why Jeff Bezos makes Amazon execs read 6-page memos

communication.text: A blog post by Slab says Stripe also rarely uses slides. Meetings begin with silent reading of a memo, followed by comments on the document.

sources.title: Slab: How Stripe Built a Writing Culture

work.text: According to the BLS, median employee tenure in January 2024 was 3.9 years overall, the lowest since January 2002. In the private sector it was 3.5 years.

sources.title: BLS: Employee Tenure in 2024

work.text: At-will employment is the default in every state except Montana. Unless the reason is illegal, either the employer or the employee can end the employment relationship at any time.

sources.title: USA.gov: Termination guidance for employers

work.text: According to layoffs.fyi figures cited by TechCrunch, tech layoffs in 2024 exceeded 150,000 people at 549 companies. The peak was 2023, with about 260,000.

sources.title: TechCrunch: A comprehensive archive of 2024 tech layoffs

work.text: In the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, 45% of US respondents work fully remote, the highest share among the top responding countries. Median salaries were $200k for engineering managers, $175k for back-end developers, and $138k for full-stack developers.

sources.title: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025: Work

work.text: In Staff Engineer (2021), Will Larson sorts Staff+ individual-contributor roles, which do not require becoming a manager, into four archetypes: Tech Lead, Architect, Solver, and Right Hand.

sources.title: Will Larson: Staff Engineer

oss.text: According to Octoverse 2025, the number of US developers on GitHub grew from 10.2 million in 2020 to 28 million in 2025, the most of any country. The US ranks second to India in open source contributors and first in total contributions.

sources.title: GitHub Octoverse 2025

oss.text: The same Octoverse 2025 report says the US, UK, and Canada more than doubled their developer counts from 2020 to 2025, while India and Brazil more than quadrupled. Its 2030 projection puts India ahead of the United States.

sources.title: GitHub Octoverse 2025

variance: Most of the evidence comes from large tech companies such as Google, Amazon, and Facebook. No data was found on how far design docs or blameless postmortems have spread in regulated industries or in corporate IT departments.
"Move fast" is often called the motto of US tech, but Facebook itself switched to "stable infra" in 2014.
Layoff trackers such as layoffs.fyi and TrueUp give counts that differ by nearly a factor of two.

Some practices described as American come from companies whose founders are not American, such as Stripe. The memo culture is better read as a practice of the US tech industry than of the country as a whole.
The Stack Overflow survey uses a self-selected sample, so its salary and work-arrangement figures depend on who chose to respond.
